milestones.label: Ulam's solitaire question
milestones.description: Ulam's 1946 idea of estimating probabilities by repeated trial, prompted by a solitaire question, is recorded as a private thought.

evidence.claim: Ulam's first thoughts on the Monte Carlo method were suggested by a question in 1946 while convalescing

milestones.note: Private idea; no dated publication, so it sets no derived date.

milestones.label: First automated Monte Carlo calculation on ENIAC
milestones.description: A fully automated Monte Carlo calculation of a fission weapon core is reported on ENIAC in spring 1948.

evidence.claim: ENIAC ran the first fully automated Monte Carlo calculation of a fission weapon core in spring 1948

milestones.note: Open: only a secondary report was checked; no primary bibliographic record was found. Derived methodological date depends on it.

milestones.label: Metropolis and Ulam publish the method
milestones.work: Metropolis, N., Ulam, S., The Monte Carlo Method, J. Amer. Statist. Assoc. 44 (1949), 335-341
milestones.description: First public statement of the method in a journal article.

evidence.claim: Metropolis, Ulam, The Monte Carlo Method, JASA 44 (1949)

milestones.label: The name in a paper title
milestones.work: Metropolis, N., Ulam, S., The Monte Carlo Method, J. Amer. Statist. Assoc. 44 (1949), 335-341
milestones.description: The title uses the name Monte Carlo for the method.

evidence.claim: Title 'The Monte Carlo Method' in JASA 1949
Metropolis suggested the code name Monte Carlo

milestones.note: Same paper as the first_statement milestone; it plays both roles, recorded as two milestones per rule 2.

milestones.label: Equation of state calculations by fast computing machines

evidence.claim: Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines, J. Chem. Phys. 1953
zbMATH record gives pages 1087-1092

milestones.note: Author list taken from the paper as cited; only the first author is in the people list here. Co-authors are not separate people entries.
